blocks.body: A tankless heater fires only when someone opens a hot tap. Water passes through a heat exchanger and comes out hot for as long as the tap is open. Because there's no tank to keep hot, it uses less energy when the house is quiet. Its limit is flow: each unit can heat only so many gallons per minute, so a large home may need a bigger unit or two units working together.

items.body: Two units piped together can serve a home with several baths running at once.
Tankless units need a lot of gas at once. The meter and line may need to be upsized.

items.h3: Lake Michigan Water Still Leaves Scale
items.body: Minerals build up in the heat exchanger over time. Yearly descaling prevents error codes and lost flow.
Some units have built-in recirculation for faster hot water at distant fixtures.

items.q: Can one tankless unit handle a large home?
items.preview: Sometimes. Larger homes often use two.
items.answer: Sometimes. If several showers and tubs run at once, two units piped together are often the better choice.

items.q: Why is my tankless unit showing an error code?
items.preview: Often scale, a dirty sensor or a venting issue.
items.answer: Often scale in the heat exchanger, a dirty flame sensor or a venting or gas supply problem. We diagnose the code and fix the cause.

items.q: How often should we descale our tankless heater?
items.answer: About once a year for most Hinsdale homes.

items.q: Can you replace an old tankless unit?
items.answer: Yes. We replace older units and update the venting and gas connections as needed.

items.q: Will a tankless unit save space in our mechanical room?
items.answer: Yes. It mounts on the wall, which frees up the floor space a tank used.

items.q: How much does a tankless water heater cost in Hinsdale?
items.preview: It depends on the unit and the gas and venting work. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the unit size, how many units you need and the gas and venting work. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
